task.description: Step 0.5/Step 1: Confirm root cause for ISS-0100 (GitHub #357). ORCH pre-investigation already found: (1) tools/clean_test_db.py ALREADY contains an unconditional `DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE tenant_type = 'production' AND slug != 'default'` sweep, present since commit 106bb44 (predates this issue) — option (a) from the issue's candidate resolution is already implemented and verified live (ran the script against db_test, 15 leaked LEGACY_RLS production rows were deleted cleanly, zero FK RESTRICT errors). (2) The actual defect is in the ISS-503 pre-flight guard (migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql, designed in src/design/iss503_rls_removal.md), which raises 'N tenant(s) still in LEGACY_RLS mode' by counting ANY row in public.tenant with storage_mode='LEGACY_RLS' — including disposable production-typed test-fixture rows created by helpers.zig/svc01/etc mid-suite, before the NEXT invocation's clean_test_db.py sweep runs. Because clean_test_db.py only runs once per `zig build` invocation (as a shared dependency via build.zig's clean_test_db_step), fixture rows inserted by one test target persist and are visible to any other check run later in the same session/build graph, or to a fresh `zig build test-integration-iss503` invocation run directly after `zig build test-integration-svc` in a separate command (each invocation reruns clean_test_db, but rows inserted during a run remain until the NEXT clean runs — so a manual/scripted verification step that queries the DB between two separate build invocations, or the pre-flight guard firing against leftover rows from a still-in-progress or crashed prior run, will see them). Confirm this diagnosis by re-reading the ISS-503 pre-flight guard SQL and by checking whether any documented CI/dev workflow runs `zig build test-integration-svc` followed directly by an ISS-503-related check WITHOUT an intervening clean-test-db (e.g. docs/agents/workflows/WF-04_full_test_run.md, package.json scripts, CI yaml). Also verify there is no separate, narrower leak: check whether `helpers.zig`'s ensureDefaultOidcSeeds() or any test in the affected-areas list creates rows that are NOT swept by the existing DELETE due to a name/slug collision with the allowlisted 'default' slug, or due to being inserted with a slug that somehow matches an exclusion. Register/update docs/issues/ISS-0100.json with the confirmed root cause (it already exists — update status if diagnosis changes anything material) and proceed to fn:register-inner-report + fn:complete-handoff. Do not implement the fix — that is Step 2/3.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed or corrected with evidence (not speculation) — must include actual command output, not assumptions
docs/issues/ISS-0100.json updated if the diagnosis differs from what's already recorded there
Clear statement of WHY the pre-flight guard (or any other consumer of public.tenant) can observe leaked rows despite clean_test_db.py already sweeping them
next_action set to route to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 2)

result.summary: Confirmed ORCH's pre-investigation and sharpened the root cause. clean_test_db.py's production-typed tenant sweep already works correctly (re-verified). The remaining defect is two compounding causes: (1) a genuine fixture-insert bug — bare INSERT INTO tenant statements across helpers.zig (ensureDefaultOidcSeeds' SVC-01..04 block) and svc01/svc04/adp07/adp04a/tenant_config_realm/oidc09-35 test files omit tenant_type (defaults 'production' per GBL-080) and storage_mode (defaults 'LEGACY_RLS' per migration 086), so every one of those rows is exactly the shape the ISS-503 guard counts; (2) migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql's pre-flight guard does not record itself as applied when it fails (per its own header comment), so TestHarness.init() retries it on every test-binary startup until it first succeeds — meaning a leaked row from an earlier test binary in the same `zig build` invocation (clean_test_db.py runs once per invocation, not between binaries) causes any later TestHarness.init() call in that invocation, including db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/02, to re-fail the same guard. No slug-collision masking bug found. Recommendation: fix the fixture inserts to set tenant_type='test' + production_tenant_id (primary), and add 'AND tenant_type = production' to the GBL-084 guard's COUNT query as defense-in-depth (supplementary). A build.zig step-ordering fix is not recommended — high blast radius, does not fix the underlying data-hygiene bug. Full evidence trail in docs/issue-reports/ISS-0100-diagnosis.yaml.
